headline: Continued decisions on 74 Main Street and Green Street Manor to November; People's Credit Union sign talks also moved to November 10.
summary: Owner Laurie Keene asked to convert second-floor storage at 39 Caswell Street into a dwelling unit. Discussion on Green Street Manor focused on fences and planting, and the People's Credit Union sign request raised questions about visibility.

plain_text:
Town of South Kingstown   
Planning Board   
Regular Session Agenda Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 6:30 PM   
South Kingstown Town Hall, Town Council Chambers 
180 High Street, Wakefield, RI 02879 
www.southkingstownri.gov  
Maria H. Mack, Chair 
Susan Axelrod, Vice Chair 
Elizabeth Karp, Secretary 
Paul Jordan 
Armand Monaco 
Robyn Pothier 
Kaiper Wilson 
 
A. Call to Order & Roll Call: 
Ms. Mack called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. 
 
ROLL CALL:  
Present: Susan Axelrod, Paul Jordan, Liz Karp, Armand Monaco, Robyn Pothier, Kaiper Wilson, and Maria Mack. 
Absent: None 
Present: James Rabbitt, Director of Planning; Brian Wagner, Deputy Director of Planning; Lynn Smith, Planning Associate; 
Mark Conboy, Town Engineer; and Peter Skwirz, Special Legal Counsel. 
B. Approval of Minutes: 
The following motion, made by Ms. Axelrod, duly seconded by Mr. Jordan, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves the Minutes as presented." 
 1. August 25, 2026 PBRS (adjusted) 
 2. September 10, 2026 PBWS 
 3. September 22, 2026 PBRS 
C. Subdivisions and Land Development Projects: 
 1. 74 Main Street - Application for Minor Land Development Project to have an accessory structure with 2 
dwelling units and Unified Development Review for waivers from street and perimeter landscaping 
requirements in the Subdivision & Land Development Regulations. Assessor's Plat 57-1, Lot 78. 
Owner/Applicant 74 Main Street, LLC. 
Laurie Keene, owner/applicant, appeared to present her application.  Ms. Keene explained that the application is for 74 
Main Street and the accessory structure at 39 Caswell Street. The property is currently comprised of her architecture 
office with one dwelling unit above, an accessory building with a first floor ADU with approved second floor storage. 
 This application is to convert the second floor storage into one additional dwelling unit, making 3 total residential units 
on the property.  Ms. Keene passed out revised plans to the Planning Board members and staff, dated October 27, 2026, 
and reviewed the changes reflected.  Ms. Keene requested the Board allow the final landscape certification to be 
provided by either a registered architect or a licensed landscape architect; as an architect herself, she would be able to 
provide that certification.   
 
Ms. Axelrod expressed concern with the application being submitted as a "minor" land development project; relief from 
zoning and or waivers would make it a "major" land development project.  Ms. Axelrod questioned why a 3-unit 
development in commercial downtown was not brought in as a major land development. Mr. Skwirz cited the statute 
45-23-32, subsection 19, with a list of qualifying projects for minor land development projects. This application would 
fall within that definition to qualify as a minor.   
 
The original ADU went through Zoning to receive a variance to have a residence on the first floor in the commercial 
downtown; the Zoning approval condition was that the second floor of the accessory structure only be used for storage. 
 The Board expressed concern that the PB was now being asked to overlook the Zoning Board's original approval
condition for the ADU.  Ms. Mack stated that it would be helpful for the Board to understand any waivers or conditions 
previously granted. Ms. Keene explained the reasoning behind the steps taken to date, and why the second floor of the 
ADU was requested as storage at that time.  Mr. Wagner reported that at TRC it was requested that one of the three 
residential units be designated as the ADU. 
 
Mr. Skwirz responded that piecemeal review can not be prevented, applications must be dealt with as they come in. 
 
When before the ZBR for relief, a condition was put on the ADU; now before the PB for relief, permitting, additional 
waivers, plus relief from the original ZBR condition.  Under the new state law, relief requiring both Zoning Board 
approval and Planning Board approval is done through a combined Unified Development Review process. Therefore, the 
Planning Board does have the authority to grant the relief with the understanding that you would need to decide to 
release the prior condition that was imposed on the ADU by the Zoning Board, of having no residential on the second 
floor. Discussion ensued. 
  
Mr. Rabbitt reported that the decision deadline is Sunday, December 6, 2026.  Mr. Rabbitt discussed issues outlined in 
the Staff Memo.  Discussion ensued regarding landscaping, overriding the Zoning Board condition, exploring why the ZB 
condition was imposed, mixed-use project requirements, site lighting, request for reduction in landscaping, buffer on 
Hazard Street, parking requirements; state legislation abolishing zoning boards, rain garden, and the catch basin/dry 
well on Caswell Street.    
 
Mr. Wagner confirmed that if the Planning Board alters the previous decision by the Zoning Board of Review, this 
application becomes a Unified Development Review and therefore, not a decision that the Administrative Officer can 
make. The deadline would then be January 4, 2027. 
 
Ms. Mack requested staff to revise the Project Memo to more thoroughly describe the process, past and present; an 
explanation of previous waivers, and how they may or may not impact the project as proposed; and the requirement for 
future waivers.  Tonight there was a discussion for the need for a landscape architect and specifics as far as size and 
species and other ways to potentially mitigate the landscape waivers as requested.     
 
The following motion, made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Ms. Karp, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby continues 74 Main Street — Minor Land Development Project to 
Tuesday, November 24, 2026." 
  2. PUBLIC HEARING: Green Street Manor - Major Multi-household Land Development Project, 
Preliminary Plan Review, located at 12 Green Street, Peace Dale, Assessor's Plat 49-1, Lot 148. To 
construct two duplexes (4 units total) with associated parking and stormwater management. 
 Jonnycake Center for Hope, applicant/owner. (Continued from September 22, 2026) 
James Callaghan, attorney for the applicant, appeared to present the project.  Mr. Callaghan stated also present were 
Kate Brewster, Jonnycake Center Executive Director; Colin Penney, Executive Director of South County Habitat for 
Humanity; and Molly Titus of DiPrete Engineering. Mr. Callaghan gave a brief history of the project to date and 
introduced the change from the Conceptual Master Plan of one building to now two.  Seeking variances, relief from the 
requirement that the first floor needs commercial space; relief to allow the proposed decks in the rear of the yard to 
extend 7.5 feet into the rear setback. Seeking two waivers for parking lot setbacks and distancing buildings.   
 
Molly Titus presented the engineering portion of the project. 
 
Colin Penney stated fences are very practical, tenants most always request a fence. He is concerned that too much of a 
tree buffer, that close to the property line, would become a maintenance nightmare. He believes there is room in the 
front of the houses for small planting beds; however, he is nervous about planting in the permeable area because of 
sight lines.    
 
Discussion ensued regarding the manhole covers in the backyard; no landscaping in front of the buildings; no buffer
between the buildings and Green Street; a few trees would be welcomed by the Planning Board; a fence along the 
western edge vs a live buffer; fences also require maintenance.  Mr. Penney stated that there are no deed restrictions 
on property now; and that deed restrictions would devalue the property; deed restrictions will come with funding.    
 
PUBLIC COMMENT:  None 
 
Staff are to meet with Jonnycake representatives this week to discuss a living fence versus a hard-scape fence; they will 
also look at the turfed area and how it could incorporate some landscaping. 
 
The following motion, made by Ms. Pothier, duly seconded by Mr. Jordan, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby continues the PUBLIC HEARING: Green Street Manor - Major 
Multi-household Land Development Project, Preliminary Plan Review to the November 10, 2026, Planning Board Work 
Session." 
D. Development Plan Review: 
 1. People's Credit Union - Application for a Change to an Approved Plan. Applicant seeks approval to modify 
the previously approved site plan to add signage to include a pylon sign and internal directional signage. 703 
Kingstown Road, Assessor's Plat 51-1, Lot 92. (Owner: People's Credit Union / Applicant: CT Sign).  
John Morrison, of Connecticut Sign Service, and Ben Tallman, head of Facilities and Security for People's Credit Union, 
appeared to represent the application. 
Mr. Morrison passed out pictures of the sign modification being requested and explained the need for the change.   
 
Discussion ensued regarding the dangers of using AI; a ground-mounted sign instead of the pylon sign being requested; 
visibility of the building; the existing building sign, the site, as purchased, is not visible from the intersection; the building 
is set back from the street; changing landscaping previously approved; and that the proposed pylon sign would be 
blocked by street tree canopy coming from the intersection.  
 
Ms. Mack requested the applicant meet with Mr. Rabbitt to discuss a resolution and/or middle ground. 
This discussion was continued to the November 10, 2026, Planning Board Work Session. 
E. Recommendations to Town Council: None 
F. Reports and Special Items: 
Ms. Mack requested a discussion on the schedule for November, December and January, particularly work sessions. 
 There are three scheduled work sessions before returning to the Town Council with any revisions to the Form Based 
Code, as they have suggested.  Mr. Rabbitt spoke about the FBC being at the November Work Session, squeezing in a 
Work Session in early December, and possibly doubling up on Work Sessions in January.   
 
Ms. Mack spoke about the Annual Action Agenda, an overview of Planning Board goals for the coming year.  The Town 
Council has recently asked the Board for an advisory on Farm Stands. Last night they asked for expertise on swimming 
pools; a bullet list for when the PB convenes in January will be helpful. 
 
Ms. Mack reminder all that November 14th is the Planning Board training at the Crown Plaza.   
 
Mr. Rabbitt stated that on November 10th, staff will have a course of action and try to lay out a schedule for the Board. 
G. Report of Administrative Officer: No actions taken/recorded in 09/2026, in accordance with RIGL. 
H. Designation of Duty Member for Next TRC Meeting - November 12, 2026 
Ms. Axelrod volunteered to attend the November 12, 2026, TRC meeting at 9:00 a.m.
I. Adjournment: 
Upon Motion made by Ms. Karp, duly seconded by Mr. Jordan, the meeting was adjourned at 8:29 p.m., by unanimous 
vote.
